title: The ark is no strange tale
source_text: Ἑξῆς δὲ τοιαῦτά φησιν· εἶτα κατακλυσμόν τινα καὶ κιβωτὸν ἀλλόκοτον, ἅπαντα ἔνδον ἔχουσαν, καὶ περιστεράν τινα καὶ κορώνην ἀγγέλους, παραχαράττοντες καὶ ῥᾳδιουργοῦντες τὸν Δευκαλίωνα· οὐ γὰρ οἶμαι προσεδόκησαν ὅτι ταῦτ᾿ εἰς φῶς πρόεισιν, ἀλλ᾿ ἀτεχνῶς παισὶ νηπίοις ἐμυθολόγησαν. καὶ ἐν τούτοις δὴ ὅρα τὴν ἀφιλόσοφον ἀπέχθειαν τοῦ ἀνδρὸς πρὸς τὴν ἀρχαιοτάτην Ἰουδαίων γραφήν. οὐ γὰρ ἔχων τὴν περὶ κατακλυσμοῦ ἱστορίαν κακολογεῖν οὐδ᾿ ἐπιστήσας οἷς ἐδύνατο λέγειν κατὰ τῆς κιβωτοῦ καὶ τῶν μέτρων αὐτῆς, καὶ ὡς οὐχ οἷόν τ᾿ ἦν κατὰ τὸν τῶν πολλῶν νοῦν ἐκλαμβάνοντα τὰ περὶ τῶν „τριακοσίων“ τοῦ μήκους „τῆς κιβωτοῦ“ „πήχεων“ „καὶ πεντήκοντα“ τοῦ πλάτους „καὶ τριάκοντα“ τοῦ ὕψους φάσκειν αὐτὴν κεχωρηκέναι τὰ ἐπὶ γῆς ζῷα, καθαρὰ μὲν ἀνὰ τέσσαρα καὶ δέκα ἀκάθαρτα δὲ ἀνὰ τέσσαρα· ἁπλῶς εἶπεν ἀλλόκοτον, πάντ᾿ ἔχουσαν ἔνδον. τί γὰρ τὸ ἀλλόκοτον αὐτῆς, ἑκατὸν ἔτεσιν ἱστορουμένης γεγενῆσθαι καὶ συναγομένης ἀπὸ τῶν „τριακοσίων“ τοῦ μήκους „πήχεων“ καὶ τῶν „πεντήκοντα“ τοῦ πλάτους, ἕως οἱ τοῦ ὕψους πήχεις „τριάκοντα“ καταλήξουσιν εἰς ἕνα πῆχυν μήκους καὶ πλάτους; πῶς δ᾿ οὐχὶ μᾶλλον θαυμαστὸν ἦν τὸ κατασκεύασμα καὶ μεγίστῃ πόλει ἐοικὸς τῷ δυνάμει λέγεσθαι τὰ μέτρα, ὡς ἐννέα μὲν εἶναι μυριάδων τὸ μῆκος κατὰ τὴν βάσιν κατὰ δὲ τὸ πλάτος δισχιλίων πεντακοσίων; πῶς δ᾿ οὐκ ἦν θαυμάσαι τὴν ἐπίνοιαν τοῦ ἐρηρεισμένην γενέσθαι καὶ δυναμένην ὑπομεῖναι χειμῶνα κατακλυσμοῦ ποιητικόν; καὶ γὰρ οὐ πίσσῃ οὐδ᾿ ἄλλῃ τινὶ τοιαύτῃ ὕλῃ, ἀσφάλτῳ δὲ στεῤῥῶς ἐκέχριστο. πῶς δ᾿ οὐ θαυμαστὸν τὸ ζώπυρα παντὸς γένους εἰσάγεσθαι ἔνδον προνοίᾳ θεοῦ. ἵν᾿ ἔχῃ πάντων σπέρματα ζῴων πάλιν ἡ γῆ, τοῦ θεοῦ δικαιοτάτῳ ἀνδρὶ χρησαμένου, πατρὶ ἐσομένῳ τῶν μετὰ τὸν κατακλυσμόν;
pass_a_gloss: Next he says such things: Then a certain flood (κατακλυσμός) and a strange (ἀλλόκοτος) ark (κιβωτός) having all things within, and a certain dove (περιστερά) and crow (κορώνη) as messengers (ἄγγελοι), counterfeiting (παραχαράττω) and tampering with (ῥᾳδιουργέω) Deucalion; for I do not think they expected (προσδοκάω) that these things would go forth into light (εἰς φῶς πρόειμι), but simply (ἀτεχνῶς) told myths (μυθολογέω) to infant children (παῖδες νήπιοι). And in these see the unphilosophical (ἀφιλόσοφος) hatred (ἀπέχθεια) of the man toward the most ancient (ἀρχαῖος, superl.) writing (γραφή) of the Jews. For not having [anything] to speak evil of (κακολογέω) the history (ἱστορία) about the flood, nor having attended (ἐφίστημι) to the things he could say against the ark and its measures (μέτρα), and that it was not possible, taking (ἐκλαμβάνω) according to the mind (νοῦς) of the many the things about the 'three hundred' 'cubits' (πῆχυς) of the length 'of the ark' 'and fifty' of the breadth 'and thirty' of the height, to say that it contained (χωρέω) the animals (ζῷα) on earth, clean (καθαρός) by fourteen each and unclean (ἀκάθαρτος) by four each; he simply (ἁπλῶς) said strange, having all things within. For what is the strange thing of it, being recorded (ἱστορέω) to have been made in a hundred years and being drawn together (συνάγω) from the 'three hundred' 'cubits' of the length and the 'fifty' of the breadth until the 'thirty' cubits of the height end (καταλήγω) into one cubit of length and breadth? And how was not rather the construction (κατασκεύασμα) wonderful (θαυμαστός) and like a greatest city, the measures being spoken in power (τῷ δυνάμει, i.e. squared), so that the length at the base (βάσις) be of nine myriads and the breadth of two thousand five hundred? And how was it not [right] to admire (θαυμάζω) the design (ἐπίνοια) of its having been made braced (ἐρείδω, pf. pass.) and able to endure (ὑπομένω) a storm (χειμών) productive (ποιητικός) of a flood? For it had been smeared (χρίω) not with pitch (πίσσα) nor any other such material (ὕλη), but firmly (στερρῶς) with asphalt (ἄσφαλτος). And how not wonderful that sparks/embers of life (ζώπυρα) of every kind (γένος) were brought in (εἰσάγω) within by providence (πρόνοια) of God, so that the earth may have again the seeds (σπέρματα) of all animals, God having used (χράομαι) a most just (δίκαιος, superl.) man, to be father of those after the flood?
pass_b_english: Next he says this: “Then a flood, and a strange ark with everything inside it (Genesis 6:14–7:16), and a dove and a crow as messengers (Genesis 8:6–12), counterfeiting and tampering with the story of Deucalion. For I do not suppose they expected that these things would come to light; they simply told myths to little children.”

Here too, see the man’s unphilosophical hatred of the most ancient Scripture of the Jews. For he could find nothing to say against the story of the flood, and he did not notice what he could have said against the ark and its measurements: that if one takes, as the many do, the statement of “three hundred cubits” for the length “of the ark,” “and fifty” for the breadth, “and thirty” for the height (Genesis 6:15), it was not possible to claim that it held the animals of the earth, the clean by fourteen of each kind and the unclean by four (Genesis 7:2–3). Instead he simply said “strange, with everything inside.”

For what is strange about it, when the record says it was a hundred years in the making, and narrowed from the three hundred cubits of its length and the fifty of its breadth until the thirty cubits of its height ended in a single cubit of length and breadth (Genesis 6:16)? Why was the structure not rather a marvel, like a very great city, since its measurements are given as squares, so that its length at the base is ninety thousand and its breadth two thousand five hundred? Why should one not admire the design that made it firmly braced and able to withstand a storm that brought on a flood? For it was smeared not with pitch or any other such material, but solidly with asphalt (Genesis 6:14). And is it not a marvel that, by the providence of God, embers of life of every kind were brought inside, so that the earth might again have the seeds of all living creatures (Genesis 7:3), God making use of a most righteous man (Genesis 6:9), who was to be the father of those who came after the flood?

choices.choice: οὐ γὰρ ἔχων: restored the dropped γάρ ('For he could find nothing to say')
τῷ δυνάμει λέγεσθαι τὰ μέτρα: 'if its measurements are taken as squares' -> 'since its measurements are given as squares' (articular infinitive, not a condition)
Celsus's words kept in quotation marks from 'Then a flood' to 'little children'; repeated phrase 'strange, with everything inside' quoted again
checked Genesis 6:9, 6:14, 6:15, 6:16, 7:2-3, 7:3, 8:6-12 against the LXX: all correct; 'a hundred years' left uncited (inferred from Genesis 5:32 and 7:6)

Celsus's words run from 'Then a flood' to 'little children'; 'strange, with everything inside' later in the chapter repeats his phrase (ἀλλόκοτον, πάντ᾿ ἔχουσαν ἔνδον) and is quoted again. The inline citations inside Celsus's sentence mark what his words allude to: the ark and its contents (Genesis 6:14–7:16) and the raven and dove (Genesis 8:6–12). Celsus says κορώνη ('crow') where the LXX has κόραξ ('raven'); Origen points this out at 4.42, so 'crow' is kept here. παραχαράττοντες = counterfeiting (a coiner's word); ῥᾳδιουργοῦντες = tampering with. Ark measurements match LXX Genesis 6:15 (300, 50, 30 cubits). 'Clean by fourteen, unclean by four' is Origen's reckoning of LXX Genesis 7:2–3 (ἑπτὰ ἑπτά = seven pairs; δύο δύο read as four); kept as he gives it. 'A hundred years in the making' is not a single verse: it is inferred from Noah's age at Genesis 5:32 (500) and Genesis 7:6 (600), so it is not cited inline. The tapering to one cubit reflects LXX Genesis 6:16 (εἰς πῆχυν συντελέσεις αὐτὴν ἄνωθεν). 'τῷ δυνάμει λέγεσθαι τὰ μέτρα' is a geometric sense ('in square'): 300 squared = 90,000 and 50 squared = 2,500; rendered 'taken as squares'; units are not named in the Greek and none are added. 'Smeared … with asphalt' answers LXX Genesis 6:14 (ἀσφαλτώσεις … τῇ ἀσφάλτῳ). 'So that the earth might again have the seeds of all living creatures' echoes Genesis 7:3 (διαθρέψαι σπέρμα ἐπὶ πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν). 'A most righteous man' alludes to Genesis 6:9 (Νωε ἄνθρωπος δίκαιος). ζώπυρα kept as Origen's image, 'embers of life'. The genitive 'τοῦ ἐρηρεισμένην γενέσθαι' after ἐπίνοιαν is construed as 'the design that made it firmly braced'. τῷ δυνάμει λέγεσθαι is an articular infinitive giving the ground (Origen holds the figures are squares), so 'since', not 'if'.
